references.text: Prohibition against swearing falsely by the Lord's name, which dishonors God's name
Parallel text to the third commandment in Deuteronomy
Command to swear only by the Lord's name, which presupposes reverence for the name
Refers to those who misuse God's name and take it in vain
Exhortation to be careful with words and vows toward God
Criticism of those who swear by the Lord's name but not in truth
God's name was profaned among the nations, and God will sanctify His name
Curse upon the one who swears falsely by the Lord's name
Jesus' teaching on not swearing falsely and keeping oaths to the Lord
The prayer 'Hallowed be your name' shows reverence for God's name
Exhortation against swearing, neither by heaven nor by earth
Creates a theological balance between God's judgment on name-abusers and His faithfulness for the sake of His name.
Connects the prohibition against name-abuse to God's zealous nature and demand for exclusive loyalty.
Expands the concept of God's honor by linking name-abuse to general mocking behavior toward God.
Links name-abuse to idolatry through the shared term 'profane God's name'.
